title: Chile’s Rising Anti-Establishment Powerbroker
gist: Franco Parisi’s Partido de la Gente (19% of the November presidential vote) has become the swing bloc that just cleared President José Antonio Kast’s corporate-tax-cutting Plan de Reconstrucción Nacional through Chile’s Senate on August 5, extracting cost-of-living concessions rather than joining the coalition. With Kast’s approval already down to 36%, the article argues PDG support is transactional and will turn confrontational as 2029 nears — Uruguay’s Cabildo Abierto (11% in 2019 to 2.5% in 2024) being the cautionary precedent for outsider parties that get absorbed.

themes.theme: PDG as Chile’s pivotal swing bloc

insights.claim: Chile’s Senate approved President Kast’s Plan de Reconstrucción Nacional on August 5, 2026, a growth bill built on corporate tax cuts and deregulation, after the lower house passed it in May with Partido de la Gente support.
insights.speaker: NICOLÁS SALDÍAS
insights.so_what: Chile’s headline corporate tax and permitting reform is now law-bound; the marginal vote on future Kast economic bills sits with a party that is not in his coalition.
insights.quote: the Senate approved the bill on August 5

insights.claim: The Partido de la Gente finished third in each of Chile’s last two presidential elections, with Franco Parisi taking 19% of the vote in November 2025 on the back of a social media following.
insights.speaker: NICOLÁS SALDÍAS
insights.so_what: A 19% third-place bloc is large enough to be the permanent price-setter for legislation in a polarized Congress — price it into any Chilean reform timeline.
insights.quote: get 19% of the vote last November
insights.locator: The Partido de la Gente (PDG) finished third

insights.claim: PDG backing for the reform bill was bought with targeted cost-of-living concessions negotiated directly between Parisi and Finance Minister Jorge Quiroz, including tax breaks for diapers and medicines.
insights.speaker: NICOLÁS SALDÍAS
insights.so_what: Expect every future Kast fiscal package to carry a consumption-relief rider; the headline pro-business measure arrives with revenue giveaways attached.
insights.quote: the government agreed to concessions that address cost of living issues including tax breaks for diapers and medicines

insights.claim: Parisi has deliberately kept the PDG outside Kast’s governing coalition, making issue-by-issue transactional bargaining, not bloc membership, the operating model for the administration’s legislative agenda.
insights.speaker: NICOLÁS SALDÍAS
insights.so_what: There is no stable governing majority to underwrite multi-year reform — each bill is repriced, which raises execution risk on the second and third tranches of the agenda.
insights.quote: The party’s posture is more pragmatic and transactional, and issue-by-issue bargaining is likely to remain its modus operandi with the Kast administration.

insights.claim: Kast’s popularity has fallen to 36% since taking office, sharply increasing his dependence on outside legislative allies.
insights.speaker: NICOLÁS SALDÍAS
insights.so_what: A 36% president paying for votes has less room to impose fiscal discipline — watch for concession creep in each successive Chilean reform bill.
insights.quote: Kast’s popularity has faded to just 36%, making the need for allies in Congress and elsewhere even more acute
insights.locator: Although Kast won last November’s election

insights.claim: Chile is described as being buffeted by rising inflation and unemployment, the macro backdrop the author expects to keep pushing Kast’s approval down.
insights.speaker: NICOLÁS SALDÍAS
insights.so_what: Deteriorating Chilean macro is not just a growth story — it is the variable that determines whether the reform coalition holds together.
insights.quote: as Chile is buffeted by rising inflation and unemployment
insights.locator: The PDG may abandon a cooperative approach

insights.claim: Kast won November 2025 on an anti-incumbent platform combining crime, migration and market-friendly reform, but Parisi came close to forcing his way into the runoff instead.
insights.speaker: NICOLÁS SALDÍAS
insights.so_what: The Chilean right’s 2025 win was narrower in structure than in headline terms; the anti-establishment vote is a live threat to the incumbent right, not only to the left.
insights.quote: Parisi was within earshot of making it to the second round
insights.locator: Although Kast won last November’s election

insights.claim: 52% of Chileans do not identify with any political party, the structural void that has let a party defining itself as ni facho ni comunacho capture a fifth of the presidential vote.
insights.speaker: NICOLÁS SALDÍAS
insights.so_what: Party-system fragmentation in Chile is structural, not cyclical — assume unstable legislative majorities as the base case through 2029.
insights.quote: 52% of the population do not identify with any party

insights.claim: Chilean disillusionment with traditional center-right and center-left parties is traced to a decade of substandard economic growth, security problems and two failed constitutional rewrites.
insights.speaker: NICOLÁS SALDÍAS
insights.so_what: The political discount on Chilean assets is a decade in the making; a single growth bill will not reverse the legitimacy deficit.
insights.quote: following a decade of substandard economic growth, security challenges and two aborted constitutional rewrites

insights.claim: Parisi built his coalition on a middle-class populism that converts affordability anxiety and blocked social mobility into resentment of the establishment, paired with a tough-on-crime stance and policies that straddle the left-right axis.
insights.speaker: NICOLÁS SALDÍAS
insights.so_what: This is the replicable Latin American outsider template — cost-of-living grievance plus security hawkishness, ideologically unclassifiable and therefore hard for incumbents to co-opt.
insights.quote: a middle-class populism that channels anxieties over affordability and frustrated social mobility into resentment of an establishment it blames for both

insights.claim: Parisi founded the PDG in 2019 and outperformed expectations in 2021 while campaigning entirely from the United States because of child support issues in Chile.
insights.speaker: NICOLÁS SALDÍAS
insights.so_what: Digital-native candidacies can now clear double-digit vote shares without physical presence or machine — traditional ground-game handicapping underprices them.
insights.quote: despite campaigning entirely from the United States because of child support issues in Chile

themes.theme: Uruguay’s Cabildo Abierto as cautionary precedent

insights.claim: Uruguay’s Cabildo Abierto collapsed from roughly 11% of the vote in 2019 (11 deputies, three senators) to 2.5% in 2024 after joining Luis Lacalle Pou’s multicolor coalition, with scandals compounding the loss of anti-establishment credibility.
insights.speaker: NICOLÁS SALDÍAS
insights.so_what: A hard, quantified base rate for what happens to outsider parties that formally ally with an incumbent: roughly a 75-80% loss of vote share in one cycle.
insights.quote: The party received just 2.5% of votes in the 2024 election.

insights.claim: Formal coalition membership, not policy disagreement, is what destroyed Cabildo Abierto’s brand — it broke ranks and pushed reforms the president rejected, yet association with a center-right administration still drained its distinctiveness.
insights.speaker: NICOLÁS SALDÍAS
insights.so_what: Explains why Parisi will stay outside Kast’s tent regardless of policy overlap — the binding constraint on Chilean legislative arithmetic is brand preservation, not ideology.
insights.quote: its association with a center-right administration drained its distinctiveness

insights.claim: Even after collapsing to 2.5%, Cabildo Abierto’s two deputies remain among the small blocs supplying the Yamandú Orsi administration the votes it needs to pass legislation.
insights.speaker: NICOLÁS SALDÍAS
insights.so_what: Fragmented legislatures give micro-blocs pricing power far beyond their vote share — a durable feature of Southern Cone legislative risk, and it now runs in Uruguay’s left-of-center direction.
insights.quote: the CA’s two deputies are among the small blocs that can supply the Yamandú Orsi administration the votes it needs to pass legislation

insights.claim: Parisi is expected to support Kast’s agenda in the short run on ideological overlap, then turn progressively more confrontational as the 2029 election approaches in order to preserve the PDG’s anti-establishment identity.
insights.speaker: NICOLÁS SALDÍAS
insights.so_what: The window for Kast to pass structural reform is front-loaded — assume legislative capacity decays sharply after the first half of the term.
insights.quote: as the 2029 election approaches, Parisi is likely to become more confrontational with Kast to preserve the PDG’s anti-establishment identity

insights.claim: The PDG could break with Kast even earlier than the 2029 calendar implies if his approval keeps sliding under rising inflation and unemployment.
insights.speaker: NICOLÁS SALDÍAS
insights.so_what: Kast’s approval print is a leading indicator for Chilean legislative risk — a further drop should be read as reform-pipeline impairment.
insights.quote: The PDG may abandon a cooperative approach even faster than expected if Kast’s approval continues to fall
insights.locator: In the short run, Parisi is likely to back

insights.claim: Polarization inside a multiparty democracy manufactures its own outsider opening: as both the center-left and center-right radicalized behind pole candidates, the voters left behind became available to a new entrant.
insights.speaker: NICOLÁS SALDÍAS
insights.so_what: A transferable screen for Latin American elections — measure how far the two poles have pulled from the center to size the space a third force can occupy.
insights.quote: Parisi’s rise shows how polarization in a multiparty democracy can create space for outsiders.

insights.claim: The author frames the binding constraint on Parisi as the transition from anti-establishment positioning to a governing agenda, which necessarily requires the compromises that destroy the positioning.
insights.speaker: NICOLÁS SALDÍAS
insights.so_what: Outsider parties face a structural trap; assume they cannot be relied on as long-term partners for multi-year policy programs anywhere in the region.
insights.quote: his challenge, like that of all similarly placed leaders and parties, is to move beyond anti-establishment positioning toward a clear governing agenda
